migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.dependency_declaration: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Direct dependencies can be declared explicitly at an appropriate project/module boundary rather than inferred from ambient state. Evidence basis: No network access in sandbox; scoring based on static inspection of program sources plus documented Go toolchain/language design properties rather than executing go build/go mod in this session. | Static language-design analysis of Go's module/build system as exercised by sampled programs under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/go/micro (mb00..mb11). | Sampled programs rely exclusively on Go standard library (fmt, math, sync, os, time); no third-party packages required. | Single first-party toolchain (go build/run/test/mod); no separate package manager or build generator needed for baseline compilation. | Dependency declarations centralized in one go.mod with deterministic go.sum lockfile, unlike multi-manifest ecosystems. | Static linking by default yields self-contained binaries with no dynamic dependency resolution at runtime. | Cross-compilation via GOOS/GOARCH needs no extra dependency packages.

metric.dependency_simplicity.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.dependency_simplicity.selection_rule: Judge language/module dependency semantics and intrinsic project dependency model. Registry size, package-manager maturity and community conventions belong to Ecosystem.

component_findings.artifact_source_separation: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Source-level program meaning is not unnecessarily tied to a single compiler ABI, filesystem convention or host-specific build assumption. Evidence basis: Assessed via static inspection of provided sample sources and documented Go toolchain/language design; did not execute cross-compilation in this sandbox session. | Static language-design analysis of Go's cross-platform build model and inspection of sampled program sources for OS/architecture-specific constructs. | Sampled sources (mb00..mb11) use only standard, platform-neutral packages (fmt, math, time, sync); no cgo, no syscall-specific code, no OS-gated build tags. | Go toolchain supports first-party cross-compilation to dozens of GOOS/GOARCH targets from a single host via env vars understood by the compiler itself -- a language/toolchain design property. | Language spec and runtime (goroutine scheduler, GC, memory model) abstract OS differences uniformly; only explicit syscall/cgo use introduces platform coupling, none present in samples. | Static linking by default (CGO_ENABLED=0) reduces dynamic-library coupling to host distributions.
